essays.question: In your opinion, should countries invest more in education? Explain why.

versions.text:
It is widely argued that national governments ought to devote a larger share of public spending to schooling. In my opinion, this is entirely justified, since greater investment in education fuels economic growth and helps to close the gap between rich and poor.

To begin with, a well-funded education system produces the skilled workforce on which a modern economy depends. Employers in sectors such as engineering, healthcare and finance increasingly seek graduates with advanced technical knowledge, digital literacy and sound problem-solving abilities. When governments allocate substantial resources to modernising classrooms and training teachers, young people acquire the competencies that the labour market actually demands. As a result, companies can recruit qualified staff more easily, unemployment falls and productivity rises. South Korea is a case in point: its sustained investment in schooling over several decades is widely seen as a key factor in its transformation into a high-income economy.

Furthermore, public investment in education plays a pivotal role in narrowing social inequality. Where schools are poorly funded, good-quality learning tends to become a privilege reserved for wealthy families, leaving talented children from disadvantaged backgrounds with limited prospects. By contrast, when the state guarantees accessible, high-quality schooling for all, young people can progress on merit rather than family income. This, in turn, strengthens social mobility and reduces long-term dependence on welfare. Finland, which offers free education and consistently achieves strong results, illustrates how equal access can benefit society as a whole.

In conclusion, I firmly believe that countries should invest more in education. Far from being a mere expense, such spending drives prosperity and creates a fairer society for future generations.

grade.summary: Đây là một bài viết xuất sắc, đạt chất lượng cao về cả nội dung lẫn hình thức trình bày. Bài viết thể hiện khả năng lập luận sắc bén, vốn từ vựng phong phú và ngữ pháp vững chắc ở mức độ cao.
weaknesses: Bài viết ở mức độ hoàn thiện cao, hầu như không có điểm yếu đáng kể nào cần khắc phục đối với một bài viết band 8.0.

feedback.taskResponse: Bài viết trả lời trực tiếp và toàn diện câu hỏi của đề bài bằng cách đưa ra lập trường rõ ràng ngay từ phần mở đầu. Các ý kiến được phát triển rất tốt với các lập luận chặt chẽ và ví dụ thực tế cụ thể như Hàn Quốc và Phần Lan.
feedback.coherenceCohesion: Bố cục bài viết mạch lạc, tuân thủ cấu trúc 4 đoạn chuẩn mực. Các từ nối và phương tiện liên kết được sử dụng tự nhiên, giúp các đoạn văn chuyển ý mượt mà và giữ vững tính logic xuyên suốt.
feedback.lexicalResource: Vốn từ vựng phong phú, sử dụng chính xác nhiều collocation tự nhiên và học thuật như 'skilled workforce', 'digital literacy', 'social mobility', và 'high-income economy'. Chính tả hoàn toàn chính xác.
feedback.grammar: Cấu trúc câu đa dạng, kết hợp linh hoạt giữa câu đơn và câu phức với các mệnh đề quan hệ và trạng ngữ chỉ điều kiện, nguyên nhân. Ngữ pháp chuẩn xác, không có lỗi sai về cấu trúc hay thì.

analysis.type_vi: Opinion: 'In your opinion, should…? Explain why.' → chọn 1 lập trường + 2 lý do

plan.step: 1. Đọc đề, chọn khung
plan.think: Đề hỏi ý kiến trực tiếp (should countries invest more…?). Chọn lập trường ủng hộ rõ ràng ngay mở bài, và chỉ 2 lý do để mỗi lý do được phát triển đủ sâu (bám Task Response), thay vì liệt kê 4–5 ý nông.

plan.step: 2. Mở bài: paraphrase + thesis
plan.think: Không chép lại đề: invest more in education → devote a larger share of public spending to schooling (đổi động từ, danh từ và chủ ngữ countries → national governments). Thesis nêu luôn 2 lý do theo đúng thứ tự sẽ triển khai (kinh tế rồi bất bình đẳng) để người đọc đi theo dễ dàng.

plan.step: 3. Lý do 1 — kinh tế
plan.think: Chọn ý phổ quát nhất cho đề đầu tư công: giáo dục → lao động có kỹ năng → doanh nghiệp tuyển dễ, thất nghiệp giảm. Đoạn đi đủ 4 bước: claim → cơ chế (ngành nào cần kỹ năng gì) → kết quả (As a result) → ví dụ. Từ 'skills' được đổi thành competencies / expertise để tránh lặp.

plan.step: 4. Lý do 2 — công bằng xã hội
plan.think: Cân bằng ý kinh tế bằng ý xã hội để bài không bị một chiều. Cơ chế: trường thiếu tiền → học tốt trở thành đặc quyền người giàu → trẻ nghèo mất cơ hội; nhà nước bảo đảm → tiến thân nhờ năng lực. Dùng 'By contrast' tạo đối lập rõ để mạch lập luận chặt (Coherence).

plan.step: 5. Ví dụ
plan.think: Dùng quốc gia có thật nhưng chỉ nói nhận định chung, không số liệu, để tránh sai sự thật. Mỗi đoạn một ví dụ khác nhau.

plan.step: 6. Kết bài
plan.think: Nhắc lại lập trường bằng từ khác rồi đóng bằng câu đảo ngược quan niệm 'chi tiêu là gánh nặng' để kết bài có ý nghĩa rộng hơn, thay vì chỉ lặp thân bài.

crossCheck.summary: Bài viết ở mức band 8.0, trả lời trọn vẹn đề bài với lập luận chặt chẽ và ví dụ thuyết phục. Điểm mạnh nổi bật là từ vựng học thuật và khả năng liên kết ý. Để tiến lên band 8.5-9, bạn cần tinh chỉnh collocation và tránh lặp từ 'schooling'.
weaknesses: Một số collocation chưa tự nhiên (sound problem-solving abilities, good-quality learning).
Từ 'schooling' bị lặp lại vài lần, có thể thay bằng 'education', 'the education system', 'schools'.
Ví dụ Hàn Quốc và Phần Lan còn khá chung chung, chưa có số liệu cụ thể để tăng tính thuyết phục.

essays.question: Discuss the role of technology in improving education.

versions.text:
Technology has become a familiar presence in modern classrooms, from interactive whiteboards to online learning platforms. This essay will explain two key ways in which it improves education: by widening access to learning and by allowing teaching to be tailored to individual needs.

First and foremost, digital technology makes learning considerably more flexible and accessible. With only a laptop and an internet connection, students in remote villages can attend live lessons, revisit recorded explanations and study at times that suit their circumstances. This convenience is particularly valuable for working adults, people with disabilities and those who live far from a university. Moreover, institutions are able to serve far larger cohorts without constructing additional buildings. Platforms such as Coursera and Khan Academy, for example, now give millions of users access to everything from school mathematics to university-level courses, often free of charge.

In addition, technology allows teaching to be adapted to the needs of each learner. In a crowded classroom, a teacher rarely has time to adjust the pace for every pupil, whereas adaptive software can identify a student's weaknesses and provide targeted practice immediately. Consequently, struggling learners receive timely support while faster ones are stretched, so overall progress becomes more even. Teachers, freed from repetitive marking, can then devote more attention to discussion and encouragement. A pupil who repeatedly makes the same grammatical error, for instance, can receive tailored exercises the same day instead of waiting weeks for feedback.

To sum up, technology improves education chiefly by broadening access and by personalising instruction. Nevertheless, it should complement rather than replace teachers, whose guidance and encouragement remain irreplaceable.

grade.summary: Bài viết của bạn đạt chất lượng tốt, bố cục chuẩn mực, lập luận sắc bén và từ vựng phong phú. Bạn đã đáp ứng hoàn toàn yêu cầu của đề bài IELTS Writing Task 2 với độ dài và nội dung thuyết phục.
weaknesses: Một số câu có xu hướng hơi dài, đôi khi có thể gây loãng nhịp nếu không ngắt nghỉ đúng chỗ.
Ví dụ về lỗi ngữ pháp ở đoạn 3 mang tính cá nhân hóa cao nhưng có thể được khái quát hóa tốt hơn để làm nổi bật luận điểm chính.

feedback.taskResponse: Bài viết trả lời tốt câu hỏi thảo luận về vai trò của công nghệ trong giáo dục, đưa ra hai luận điểm rõ ràng là mở rộng khả năng tiếp cận và cá nhân hóa việc học. Các ý được phát triển mạch lạc với ví dụ cụ thể như Coursera và Khan Academy.
feedback.coherenceCohesion: Bố cục bài viết hoàn chỉnh với 4 đoạn rõ ràng. Các liên kết từ (First and foremost, Moreover, In addition, Consequently, To sum up) được sử dụng linh hoạt và tự nhiên giúp người đọc theo dõi mạch văn tốt.
feedback.lexicalResource: Vốn từ vựng phong phú, sử dụng nhiều cụm từ học thuật chính xác (accessible, tailored to individual needs, flexible, adaptive software, targeted practice). Chính tả và cách kết hợp từ (collocations) rất tốt.
feedback.grammar: Cấu trúc ngữ pháp đa dạng, kết hợp linh hoạt giữa câu đơn và câu phức (whereas, while, whose). Các lỗi ngữ pháp rất hiếm và câu văn trôi chảy, đúng chuẩn văn phong nghị luận học thuật.

analysis.type_vi: Opinion dạng 'Discuss the role of X in Y' → trình bày 2 vai trò (không phải tranh luận hai phe)

plan.step: 1. Nhận diện dạng đề
plan.think: 'Discuss the role of technology in improving education' không hỏi đồng ý hay không, mà hỏi công nghệ đóng vai trò gì. Vì vậy dùng khung vai trò: mở bài báo trước 2 vai trò, mỗi thân bài một vai trò, kết bài thêm một lưu ý để bài cân bằng.

plan.step: 2. Mở bài
plan.think: Câu 1 đặt bối cảnh bằng hình ảnh cụ thể (bảng tương tác, nền tảng học online) thay vì câu sáo 'In today's world'. Câu 2 báo trước đúng 2 vai trò theo đúng thứ tự sẽ viết.

plan.step: 3. Vai trò 1 — mở rộng tiếp cận
plan.think: Ý phổ quát nhất của edtech: linh hoạt thời gian / địa điểm, phục vụ nhóm bị loại trừ (người đi làm, vùng xa, người khuyết tật). Thêm cơ chế phía tổ chức (phục vụ nhiều học viên không cần xây thêm), rồi ví dụ nền tảng có thật.

plan.step: 4. Vai trò 2 — cá nhân hoá
plan.think: Đối lập lớp đông (giáo viên không chỉnh nhịp cho từng em) với phần mềm thích ứng. Kết quả hai chiều: em yếu được hỗ trợ kịp, em nhanh được thử thách, giáo viên thoát khỏi chấm bài lặp lại.

plan.step: 5. Kết bài có lưu ý
plan.think: Tóm tắt 2 vai trò rồi thêm 1 câu 'nhưng': công nghệ bổ trợ chứ không thay thế giáo viên. Câu lưu ý này làm bài trông cân nhắc và an toàn với mọi đề về công nghệ.

crossCheck.summary: Bài viết hoàn thành tốt yêu cầu đề, đưa ra hai luận điểm rõ ràng và có tính thuyết phục. Từ vựng và ngữ pháp ở mức tốt, bố cục mạch lạc. Để đạt band cao hơn, có thể bổ sung phân tích sâu hơn về vai trò bổ trợ của công nghệ và mở rộng góc nhìn phản biện nếu đề bài yêu cầu.
weaknesses: Chưa thảo luận sâu các hạn chế hoặc quan điểm đối lập (nếu đề yêu cầu discuss).
Một vài lựa chọn từ chưa tối ưu về sắc thái học thuật ('faster ones', 'convenience').
Liên kết từ còn hơi lặp lại, có thể đa dạng hơn.

essays.question: To what extent should media studies be taught in schools? Give reasons for your answer.

versions.text:
Young people today spend a large part of their lives consuming news, advertisements and entertainment through screens. I largely agree that media studies should form part of the school curriculum, since it teaches pupils to evaluate information critically and prepares them for a media-driven world of work.

To begin with, media studies equips pupils to distinguish reliable information from misleading content. Social media platforms deliver a constant stream of news, opinion and rumour, and false claims often spread faster than corrections. Pupils who learn to check sources, identify bias and recognise emotional manipulation are far less likely to be deceived or to share misinformation. Such analytical habits also protect them as future voters, who must judge political messages that are designed to persuade rather than inform. A teenager who has analysed how a misleading headline is constructed, for example, will find it easier to question a viral post during an election campaign.

Furthermore, the subject builds practical skills with clear career value. Advertising, journalism, film and digital marketing are major industries, and even employees in unrelated fields must now communicate effectively through video, social media and online platforms. By producing short films, blogs or campaigns, pupils learn to plan, collaborate and present ideas to an audience. They also begin to understand how advertisers target young consumers, which helps them to make more informed choices about what they buy. However, media studies should not replace core subjects such as mathematics and literacy; it works best as a focused course within a balanced timetable.

In conclusion, I believe that schools should teach media studies because it develops critical judgement and employable skills, provided that it is integrated sensibly into the existing curriculum.

grade.summary: Bài viết có chất lượng tốt, lập luận chặt chẽ, bố cục rõ ràng và ngôn ngữ tự nhiên. Người viết đã trả lời trọn vẹn yêu cầu đề bài với văn phong học thuật phù hợp.

Cách diễn đạt đôi khi hơi an toàn, chưa thực sự bứt phá lên mức band 8.5-9.0 về từ vựng.

feedback.taskResponse: Bài viết trả lời tốt câu hỏi 'To what extent' bằng cách đưa ra quan điểm đồng tình phần lớn và cân bằng bằng việc giới hạn phạm vi môn học ở đoạn 3. Các ý được phát triển đầy đủ và có ví dụ minh họa rõ ràng.
feedback.coherenceCohesion: Bố cục bài viết mạch lạc với phần mở đầu, các đoạn thân bài có câu chủ đề rõ ràng và phần kết luận tóm tắt tốt. Các từ nối được sử dụng tự nhiên và hiệu quả.
feedback.lexicalResource: Vốn từ vựng phong phú, sử dụng chính xác các cụm từ chủ đề như 'misinformation', 'emotional manipulation', 'media-driven world of work'. Tuy nhiên, có thể bổ sung thêm một số từ vựng nâng cao hơn nữa để đạt band 8+.
feedback.grammar: Cấu trúc câu đa dạng, từ câu đơn đến câu phức được sử dụng linh hoạt với độ chính xác cao. Ngữ pháp không có lỗi lớn, thể hiện sự kiểm soát cấu trúc tốt.

analysis.type_vi: Extent: 'To what extent should X be taught in schools?' → lập trường 'largely agree' + giới hạn

plan.step: 1. Đọc chữ 'to what extent'
plan.think: Đề hỏi mức độ, nên không nói 'tuyệt đối đồng ý' mà chọn 'largely agree' và dành một câu giới hạn ở thân bài 2 (không thay môn cốt lõi). Câu giới hạn này chính là câu trả lời cho 'extent', giúp Task Response đủ điểm.

plan.step: 2. Mở bài
plan.think: Mở bằng bối cảnh gần gũi (giới trẻ tiêu thụ tin tức qua màn hình), không chép đề. Thesis nêu 2 lý do: đánh giá thông tin phản biện + chuẩn bị cho thế giới việc làm bị truyền thông chi phối.

plan.step: 3. Lý do 1 — phân biệt thông tin
plan.think: Ý cốt lõi của môn truyền thông: thông tin giả lan nhanh hơn đính chính → học sinh biết kiểm tra nguồn thì khó bị lừa → cử tri tốt hơn. Ví dụ giả định về tiêu đề gây hiểu lầm trong mùa bầu cử.

plan.step: 4. Lý do 2 — kỹ năng nghề nghiệp + giới hạn
plan.think: Ngành quảng cáo, báo chí, tiếp thị số là ngành lớn; mọi nghề giờ đều cần giao tiếp qua kênh số. Sau đó thêm 'However' để giới hạn: môn này không thay toán và ngôn ngữ, chỉ là khoá tập trung trong thời khoá biểu cân đối.

plan.step: 5. Kết bài có điều kiện
plan.think: Lặp lại lập trường kèm điều kiện 'provided that…' khớp với câu giới hạn ở thân bài 2.

crossCheck.summary: Bài viết tốt, đạt mức 8.0 tổng thể. Lập luận rõ ràng, từ vựng và ngữ pháp vững. Để lên band 8.5, thí sinh cần tăng thêm độ tinh tế trong lập luận và dùng từ vựng đặc sắc hơn.

Từ vựng tuy tốt nhưng chưa có nhiều cụm từ đặc sắc band 8.5+

essays.question: Do the advantages of online learning outweigh the disadvantages? Give reasons and examples.

versions.text:
Online learning has expanded rapidly over the past decade, and many students now follow entire degrees through a screen. Although it has certain drawbacks, I believe that its benefits clearly outweigh them.

On the positive side, online learning makes education far more flexible and affordable. Students can attend lessons from any location, replay difficult explanations and arrange their studies around jobs or family responsibilities. In addition, learners save on commuting, accommodation and printed textbooks, while institutions save on buildings and staff, so fees can be kept lower. As a result, people who might otherwise be excluded, such as rural residents and working parents, are able to gain qualifications. A nurse who studies for a master's degree in the evenings, for instance, can improve her career prospects without giving up her income.

On the negative side, online study carries the risk of distraction and reduced human contact. Devices offer endless temptations such as games and social media, and learners who study alone miss the encouragement, discipline and immediate feedback that a teacher provides in person. Furthermore, families without a reliable internet connection or a suitable device may fall behind, which could deepen existing inequalities. Nevertheless, these problems are far from insurmountable. Schools can arrange live sessions, regular check-ins and loan schemes for laptops, and learners can develop self-discipline through structured timetables.

In conclusion, despite the risks of distraction and unequal access, online learning is, on balance, more beneficial than harmful, thanks to its flexibility and lower cost. With proper support, its drawbacks can largely be overcome.

grade.summary: Đây là một bài viết hoàn chỉnh và xuất sắc về mặt cấu trúc cũng như lập luận cho dạng đề Advantages / Disadvantages. Bài viết đạt độ dài trên 255 từ, thể hiện khả năng tư duy mạch lạc và vốn từ vựng, ngữ pháp vững chắc ở mức band 7.5-8.0.
weaknesses: Một số ý ở phần thân bài có thể được đào sâu hơn nữa về mặt phân tích tác động dài hạn.
Cách diễn đạt đôi chỗ còn hơi an toàn, chưa có nhiều từ vựng thực sự học thuật bậc cao (C1/C2).

feedback.taskResponse: Bài viết trả lời tốt câu hỏi của đề bài, có lập trường rõ ràng từ đầu đến cuối. Các ưu và nhược điểm được phân tích đầy đủ kèm theo ví dụ thực tế.
feedback.coherenceCohesion: Bố cục bài viết rất rành mạch với các đoạn văn rõ ràng. Các từ nối và phương tiện liên kết được sử dụng mượt mà, giúp người đọc dễ theo dõi.
feedback.lexicalResource: Từ vựng phong phú, sử dụng nhiều cụm từ tự nhiên và chính xác liên quan đến giáo dục trực tuyến. Chính tả và cách kết hợp từ (collocation) rất tốt.
feedback.grammar: Cấu trúc câu đa dạng, từ câu đơn đến câu phức đều được kiểm soát tốt. Ngữ pháp chính xác gần như tuyệt đối, không có lỗi lặp cấu trúc đáng kể.

analysis.type_vi: Advantages / Disadvantages: 'Do the advantages outweigh the disadvantages?' → chọn phe 'ưu điểm thắng'

plan.step: 1. Chọn phe và khung

essays.question: Some people prefer traditional classrooms while others prefer online learning. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

versions.text:
People hold different views on whether traditional classrooms provide the better learning environment or whether online learning is preferable. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of traditional classrooms emphasise the value of face-to-face interaction. Learning in a physical classroom fosters teamwork, shared responsibility and contact with peers who hold different viewpoints, qualities that are difficult to develop through a screen. A teacher who is present can read facial expressions, notice confusion and adjust an explanation instantly. Moreover, a fixed timetable and a dedicated learning space encourage discipline, particularly among younger children who lack the self-control to study alone. For example, pupils who complete a group project learn to negotiate disagreements rather than avoid them.

On the other hand, advocates of online learning point to its flexibility and accessibility. With a laptop and an internet connection, students can attend lessons from remote areas, revisit recorded explanations and study at times that suit their personal circumstances. This convenience widens participation, especially among working adults and people with health conditions who might otherwise be excluded. In addition, online courses are often more affordable, since learners save on travel and accommodation. Platforms such as Coursera and Khan Academy, for instance, give millions of users access to lessons at little or no cost.

In conclusion, both approaches have genuine merits. Personally, I believe that a blended model, with face-to-face teaching as its foundation and online tools as a supplement, offers the most effective approach, since it combines human interaction with flexibility.

essays.question: To what extent should critical thinking be taught in schools? Give reasons for your answer.

versions.text:
Critical thinking, the ability to question assumptions and weigh evidence, is often praised but rarely taught explicitly. I largely agree that it should be a core element of schooling, since it deepens learning and equips young people to cope with an overload of information.

To begin with, teaching critical thinking encourages pupils to understand ideas instead of merely memorising facts. When learners are expected to question, compare and justify their views, they grasp concepts more thoroughly and retain them for far longer. This capacity for independent reasoning is invaluable at university and in the workplace, where problems rarely come with a ready-made answer. Recruiters, for instance, consistently seek graduates who can analyse a situation, evaluate alternatives and defend a decision, rather than those who can only repeat what they have been taught. A student who has debated two sides of a historical event in class will find it easier to build a coherent argument in a later essay or meeting.

Furthermore, critical thinking is the best defence against misleading information. Pupils today encounter news, rumours and advertisements online every day, and false claims often spread faster than corrections. Those who have learned to check sources, spot bias and test an argument for logical weaknesses are far less likely to be deceived, and they become more responsible citizens when they vote or share content. However, schools need not create a separate subject: the skill is best developed within existing lessons such as science, history and literature, so that the timetable is not overloaded.

In conclusion, I believe that critical thinking deserves a central place in the curriculum because it improves understanding and protects pupils from manipulation, provided that it is woven into everyday teaching rather than added as another burden.

essays.question: Is it better to focus government spending on education or on other priorities? Discuss and give your opinion.

versions.text:
Opinions are divided as to whether education should be the priority for public spending or whether other sectors deserve a larger share of the budget. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, those who put education first argue that it is the foundation of long-term national development. A well-funded school system produces graduates with the skills that modern industries require, which raises productivity, attracts investment and widens the tax base. Education also narrows the gap between rich and poor, since talented children from low-income families can progress on merit rather than family wealth. Countries that expanded access to schooling after the Second World War, such as South Korea, later enjoyed rapid economic growth.

On the other hand, critics point out that governments have limited funds and many equally urgent responsibilities. Hospitals, public transport, housing and social care all demand substantial investment, and a shortage of hospital beds or a failing road network can cost lives and damage the economy immediately. Moreover, spending more on education does not guarantee better results if money is wasted on poorly designed programmes, whereas a modest sum directed at the right area, such as healthcare for an ageing population, may bring greater benefit. A rural region with no emergency hospital, for example, has more pressing needs than new school equipment.

In conclusion, although other public services deserve adequate funding, I believe that education should come first, because a well-educated population ultimately generates the revenue and expertise that sustain every other service.

essays.question: Some people say that children should learn coding at school. Do you agree or disagree?

versions.text:
Programming is no longer a specialist skill confined to software companies, and a growing number of people believe that children should learn to code at school. I firmly agree with this view, since coding develops logical problem-solving and prepares young people for a job market driven by software.

To begin with, learning to code cultivates computational thinking, that is, the habit of breaking a complex problem into smaller, logical steps. When pupils write a program, they must spell out every instruction precisely and then trace their own logic to discover why it fails. Debugging in this way builds patience, attention to detail and cause-and-effect reasoning, skills that transfer to mathematics, science and everyday decision-making. Unlike memorising facts, it shows learners that mistakes are a normal and useful part of reaching a solution. A pupil whose simple game keeps freezing, for instance, has to examine the code line by line instead of guessing at the cause.

Furthermore, coding prepares children for a world in which software underpins almost every industry. Finance, healthcare, design and even farming now rely on programs that analyse data and automate routine tasks, so employees who understand how such tools work have a clear advantage. Even pupils who never become software engineers will be better able to use, question and adapt the technology that shapes their working lives. An accountant who can write a short script to process thousands of invoices, for example, finishes in minutes what once took days. Admittedly, schools must provide trained teachers and suitable equipment, but this cost is modest compared with the benefits.

In conclusion, I am convinced that coding deserves a place in the school curriculum because it builds both a logical mind and the digital competence that the future will demand.

essays.question: To what extent do you agree or disagree that homework should be banned?

versions.text:
Whether homework should be abolished is a question that divides parents, teachers and researchers alike. I agree that it should be banned, since it deprives children of rest and play and puts pupils from disadvantaged homes at a further disadvantage.

To begin with, setting homework robs children of the rest, play and family time that healthy development depends on. After six hours in class, many pupils face another two or three hours of written tasks, so sleep is cut short and hobbies are abandoned. Exhausted children absorb less in the following day's lessons, which defeats the purpose of the extra work. Resentment also builds, and some come to associate learning with chores rather than curiosity. A child who finishes worksheets at ten o'clock at night, for example, arrives at school drained the next morning.

Furthermore, restricting learning to school hours would make education fairer. At home, children from crowded or noisy households, or with parents who cannot explain difficult tasks, are at a clear disadvantage compared with classmates who have a quiet desk and a private tutor. Completing work in class, under the teacher's supervision, gives everyone the same conditions and the same support, and teachers receive an accurate picture of what each pupil can do unaided. Some argue that homework teaches self-discipline, but this skill can equally be developed through supervised independent study during the school day. A pupil whose parents work night shifts, for instance, has no one to explain a confusing mathematics exercise.

In conclusion, I believe that homework should be abolished, provided that schools use the time saved for supervised practice, because this approach protects children's wellbeing and gives every pupil an equal chance to succeed.

essays.question: Discuss how education influences economic development.

versions.text:
Education is widely regarded as a cornerstone of economic progress. This essay will outline two principal ways in which schooling influences a country's development: by creating a productive workforce and by reducing the social costs that hold economies back.

First and foremost, education supplies the human capital that modern economies need. Employers in sectors such as engineering, healthcare and finance increasingly seek workers with advanced technical knowledge, digital literacy and sound judgement, and each additional year of schooling generally makes an employee more productive and better paid. As a result, businesses grow, tax revenues rise and governments can finance infrastructure and public services. In addition, educated citizens are more likely to start companies and develop new technologies, which creates jobs and attracts investment. Singapore, a small country with few natural resources, is often cited as a nation that built its prosperity chiefly on the quality of its schools and universities.

Beyond personal advancement, education also reduces costs that would otherwise drain public budgets. Educated individuals are statistically more inclined to make healthier lifestyle choices and less prone to criminal behaviour, which eases the burden on hospitals, police and prisons. Moreover, better-informed citizens are able to plan their finances, save for retirement and avoid long-term unemployment, so fewer rely on welfare. A community in which most residents have completed secondary school, for example, typically reports lower crime and healthier habits, leaving more public money available for investment.

To sum up, education drives economic development both by building a skilled, innovative workforce and by lowering the social costs of ill health and crime. For these reasons, it deserves sustained public support.

essays.question: Do the advantages of studying abroad outweigh the disadvantages? Give reasons and examples.

versions.text:
Increasing numbers of students now choose to complete part or all of their degree overseas. Although studying abroad involves financial and emotional challenges, I believe that its advantages outweigh them.

On the positive side, studying abroad broadens students' horizons and improves their employability. Living in another country immerses them in a foreign language every day, so their fluency develops far more quickly than it would in a classroom at home. They also learn to adapt to unfamiliar customs, work with people from different backgrounds and solve everyday problems independently, qualities that multinational employers value highly. In addition, the friendships and professional networks formed overseas often lead to opportunities later in life. A graduate who is fluent in two languages and has lived abroad, for example, may apply for positions in several countries, which multiplies her career options.

On the negative side, studying overseas places a heavy burden on individuals, both financially and emotionally. Tuition, accommodation and living expenses can consume a family's savings, while homesickness and unfamiliar surroundings leave some students isolated and struggling. Consequently, those who cannot cope may return with debts and disappointing results. Nevertheless, these difficulties can be reduced. Many universities offer scholarships, part-time work permits and counselling services for international students, and those who choose their destination carefully and plan their budget in advance are far better prepared to cope.

In conclusion, despite the high costs and the emotional strain, studying abroad is, on balance, more beneficial than harmful, thanks to the language skills, independence and career opportunities that it offers.

versions.text:
Increasing numbers of students now choose to complete part or all of their degree overseas. Although studying abroad involves financial and emotional challenges, I believe that its advantages outweigh them.

On the positive side, studying abroad broadens students' horizons and improves their employability. Living in another country immerses them in a foreign language every day, so their fluency develops far more quickly than it would in a classroom at home. They also learn to adapt to unfamiliar customs, work with people from different backgrounds and solve everyday problems independently, qualities that multinational employers value highly. Such confidence is hard to acquire in a lecture hall at home. In addition, the friendships and professional networks formed overseas often lead to opportunities later in life. A graduate who is fluent in two languages and has lived abroad, for example, may apply for positions in several countries, which multiplies her career options.

On the negative side, studying overseas places a heavy burden on individuals, both financially and emotionally. Tuition, accommodation and living expenses can consume a family's savings, while homesickness and unfamiliar surroundings leave some students isolated and struggling. Consequently, those who cannot cope may return with debts and disappointing results. Nevertheless, these difficulties can be reduced. Many universities offer scholarships, part-time work permits and counselling services for international students, and those who choose their destination carefully and plan their budget in advance are far better prepared to cope. Careful research into courses, living costs and available support before departure also reduces unpleasant surprises.

In conclusion, despite the high costs and the emotional strain, studying abroad is, on balance, more beneficial than harmful, thanks to the language skills, independence and career opportunities that it offers.

essays.question: To what extent do you agree or disagree that tests and exams accurately measure intelligence?

versions.text:
Examinations have been the main way of judging students for generations, and some people claim that they give an accurate measure of intelligence. I strongly disagree with this view, since tests capture only a narrow range of abilities and their results are easily distorted by pressure and unequal preparation.

To begin with, relying on examinations gives only a narrow picture of ability. Written tests mainly reward memory and speed under timed conditions, while creativity, teamwork, leadership and practical skills go unmeasured. Consequently, talented individuals who simply perform poorly in exam halls may be unfairly labelled as weak, and teaching tends to drift towards test preparation instead of genuine understanding. A gifted artist or entrepreneur, for example, may leave school with unimpressive grades despite exceptional real-world potential.

Furthermore, exam results are heavily influenced by factors that have little to do with intelligence. High-stakes tests tend to place students under excessive and prolonged pressure, so anxiety, sleepless nights and fear of failure can lower the performance of even very capable candidates. In addition, pupils whose families can afford private tutors enjoy a clear advantage over equally able classmates who cannot. Admittedly, examinations provide a standard that is easy to compare, but being easy to compare is not the same as being accurate. Assessment that combines coursework, projects and presentations over a longer period would give a fairer and fuller picture.

In conclusion, I cannot accept that exams accurately measure intelligence, given their narrow focus and their sensitivity to stress and family wealth.

essays.question: Some argue that early childhood education is the most important stage. To what extent do you agree?

versions.text:
Many educationalists argue that early childhood education is the most crucial stage of schooling. I largely agree with this view, since the early years lay the foundations for all later learning and offer the most effective way of reducing inequality.

To begin with, young children's brains develop with extraordinary speed, so the experiences they have before the age of six shape their later ability to learn. Through play, stories and simple group activities, children acquire language, curiosity and the habit of concentrating, and these skills allow them to benefit fully from primary school. By contrast, those who start formal schooling without them often struggle to catch up and lose confidence in their own ability. A child who has been read to daily and encouraged to ask questions, for example, usually learns to read earlier and with greater enjoyment.

Furthermore, high-quality early education is the most efficient tool for closing the gap between rich and poor. Children from disadvantaged families often begin school already behind their peers in vocabulary and social skills, and the gap tends to widen each year unless something is done early. Providing affordable nurseries and trained staff therefore helps all children to start on an equal footing, and it costs far less than remedial programmes in later years. That said, later stages remain essential: secondary and university education provide the specialist knowledge that careers require, so early learning should be seen as the foundation rather than the whole structure.

In conclusion, early childhood education is, to a large extent, the most important stage because it shapes a child's future learning and gives every child a fair start.

essays.question: Discuss the role of libraries in modern society.

versions.text:
Libraries are sometimes dismissed as relics of the pre-internet age, yet they remain a familiar feature of most towns and cities. This essay will outline two roles that they continue to play in modern society: providing free access to knowledge and acting as a hub for the community.

First and foremost, libraries give everyone access to information regardless of income. Books, newspapers, e-books and databases that would cost a great deal to buy individually are available free of charge, while public computers and internet connections serve residents who have none at home. This is especially valuable for job seekers, students from low-income families and older people, who might otherwise be excluded from the digital world. Moreover, librarians help visitors to find reliable sources, a skill that becomes more important as online misinformation spreads. A student who cannot afford textbooks, for example, can still complete a research project by borrowing materials and using the library's databases.

In addition, libraries function as community hubs that bring people together. They provide quiet study spaces, children's story sessions, language classes for newcomers and workshops on subjects ranging from computing to health, so they nurture a reading habit from an early age and strengthen social bonds across generations. For many isolated residents, such as retired people living alone, a weekly book club may be their main source of company. By adapting to modern needs, through digital lending and flexible opening hours, libraries therefore remain relevant rather than obsolete.

To sum up, libraries play a vital role by offering equal access to knowledge and by serving as meeting places that strengthen communities. For these reasons, they deserve continued public support.

essays.question: Some people say that university degrees are less valuable now. Do you agree or disagree?

versions.text:
Rising tuition fees and the success of entrepreneurs who never graduated have led some people to claim that university degrees are less valuable than they once were. I disagree with this view, since a degree still opens doors to well-paid careers and develops abilities that employers continue to demand.

To begin with, a degree remains the gateway to many professions. Doctors, engineers, architects and teachers cannot practise without recognised qualifications, and in other fields employers routinely use a degree to screen applicants when hundreds apply for a single vacancy. Statistically, graduates also tend to earn more and face lower unemployment over their working lives than those with only school-level qualifications. As a result, the financial benefit usually outweighs the cost in the long term. A graduate engineer, for instance, can expect far wider opportunities than someone who left school without a technical qualification.

Furthermore, university teaches skills that go beyond a particular subject. Students learn to research independently, analyse evidence, meet deadlines and communicate ideas clearly, abilities that remain useful when technology changes the content of jobs. They also form friendships and professional networks that often lead to opportunities later. Admittedly, some successful people in the technology industry left university early, and trades such as plumbing offer secure incomes without a degree, but these examples are exceptions rather than the rule. For most young people, a degree still provides the most reliable route to a stable career.

In conclusion, I do not believe that degrees have lost their value, because they continue to unlock professions and to build skills that employers prize.

essays.question: How can governments encourage reading among children? Suggest practical measures.

versions.text:
Reading for pleasure has declined among children in many countries, as screens compete for their attention. This essay will suggest practical measures that governments could take, focusing on access to books and on building a lasting reading habit.

First and foremost, governments should make books easy to obtain for every child. Many families on low incomes cannot afford to buy books regularly, so funding for well-stocked school and public libraries is essential, and mobile libraries could reach rural communities where there are no bookshops. Free book-gifting schemes, in which every newborn or school starter receives age-appropriate titles, would also put books into homes where there are few. Schemes such as Bookstart in the United Kingdom, for instance, give free books to families with young children to encourage reading from an early age. Such investment is modest compared with the long-term benefits, since children who read widely generally achieve better results across all subjects.

In addition, authorities should help children to enjoy reading rather than treat it as a chore. Schools could be required to set aside a short daily reading period and to let pupils choose books that match their interests, since enjoyment, not obligation, creates lasting habits. Authors' visits, reading challenges with small rewards and national campaigns featuring popular sportspeople as role models would make reading appear attractive. Furthermore, parents should be encouraged, through workshops and free advice, to read with their children at home, as children who see adults reading are more likely to imitate them. A boy who dislikes novels, for example, may become an enthusiastic reader once offered a book about his favourite football team.

In conclusion, expanding access to books and making reading enjoyable through schools, campaigns and families offer the most realistic way of encouraging children to read.

essays.question: Discuss the role of museums in education.

versions.text:
Museums are sometimes seen as places for tourists rather than for learners, yet they play a valuable part in education. This essay will outline two key contributions: bringing subjects to life through real objects, and promoting cultural understanding among people of all ages.

First and foremost, museums make abstract subjects tangible. Pupils who handle replicas, watch demonstrations and examine genuine artefacts understand history and science far better than those who only read about them in textbooks, because seeing and touching engages several senses at once. Interactive exhibits also encourage visitors to ask questions and draw their own conclusions, which develops curiosity and independent thinking. Moreover, trained guides can adapt explanations to different ages, so that a single exhibition serves both young children and university students. A class studying ancient Egypt, for example, will remember the daily lives of ordinary people far more vividly after seeing real tools, jewellery and mummies than after a lesson based on text.

In addition, museums promote cultural understanding and lifelong learning. Collections drawn from different regions and periods let visitors appreciate traditions other than their own, which weakens prejudice and strengthens respect between communities. Because many museums are free or inexpensive, and increasingly offer online tours and resources, they are accessible to people of all ages and incomes, including adults who wish to learn after leaving school. By contrast, a classroom reaches only its enrolled students. A retired visitor attending a weekend lecture on local history, for instance, may gain as much from the museum as any schoolchild.

To sum up, museums contribute to education by making learning vivid and by encouraging cultural awareness throughout life. For these reasons, they deserve continued public support.

analysis.type_vi: Opinion dạng 'Discuss the role of X in education' → 2 vai trò (cùng khung với đề thư viện 83)

plan.think: Đề 'role of museums in education' giống 'role of libraries in modern society'. Dùng lại: mở bài dạng 'X is sometimes seen as…, yet…', báo trước 2 vai trò, 2 thân bài, kết bài kêu gọi hỗ trợ công. Chỉ phải nghĩ nội dung riêng cho bảo tàng.

plan.step: 2. Vai trò 1 — học bằng vật thật
plan.think: Điểm riêng của bảo tàng là vật thật và tương tác: chạm, nhìn, thử nghiệm huy động nhiều giác quan; câu hỏi và tự kết luận phát triển tư duy; hướng dẫn viên điều chỉnh theo độ tuổi. Ví dụ lớp học Ai Cập cổ đại. Tái sử dụng ý 'tư duy độc lập' từ đề 20.

crossCheck.summary: Bài viết chất lượng tốt, trả lời đúng đề và có lập luận rõ ràng với ví dụ thuyết phục. Điểm yếu chính nằm ở một lỗi ngữ pháp nhỏ và vài cụm collocation chưa tự nhiên. Nhìn chung bài viết tương đương band 8.0 nếu khắc phục lỗi ngữ pháp.

Đại từ 'them' trong câu so sánh hơi mơ hồ.

essays.question: Some argue that technology in schools improves learning. To what extent do you agree?

versions.text:
Computers, tablets and interactive whiteboards are now standard equipment in many schools. I largely agree that this technology improves learning, provided that it is used purposefully rather than for its own sake.

To begin with, digital tools make lessons more engaging and help pupils to grasp difficult concepts. Simulations allow a physics class to test how a bridge behaves under different loads, and animations can show a chemical reaction or a historical battle in ways that diagrams on a page cannot. Interactive quizzes and educational games provide instant feedback, so pupils see immediately what they have misunderstood, and the element of competition keeps many reluctant learners motivated. Students who are involved in a lesson tend to concentrate longer and remember more. A geography class that explores a volcano through a three-dimensional model, for instance, gains a clearer picture than one that relies solely on a textbook photograph.

Furthermore, technology allows teachers to tailor instruction to individual pupils. In a crowded classroom, a teacher rarely has time to adjust the pace for every child, whereas adaptive software can identify weaknesses and provide targeted practice at once. As a result, struggling pupils receive timely support while faster ones are stretched, and teachers, freed from repetitive marking, can devote more attention to discussion. However, technology is only a tool: without proper teacher training and clear learning goals, tablets may become expensive distractions. Its benefits therefore depend on how it is used.

In conclusion, technology improves learning by making lessons more vivid and more personalised, but only when teachers use it with a clear educational purpose.

analysis.type_vi: Extent: 'technology in schools improves learning. To what extent do you agree?' → largely agree + giới hạn

plan.step: 1. Khung Extent + câu giới hạn quen thuộc
plan.think: Đề Extent (giống 9, 20, 70) nên dùng 'largely agree' và câu giới hạn ở thân bài 2. Với công nghệ, giới hạn chuẩn là 'chỉ là công cụ, cần đào tạo giáo viên và mục tiêu rõ'.

plan.step: 3. Lý do 1 — bài học sinh động, hiểu khái niệm khó (ý mới, riêng cho lớp học)

essays.question: Many people think that music education benefits children. Do you agree? Explain with examples.

versions.text:
Music is often regarded as an optional extra in the school timetable, but I firmly agree that music education benefits children, since it strengthens their intellectual skills and supports their emotional and social development.

To begin with, learning an instrument trains the mind. Reading notation, memorising pieces and coordinating hands, eyes and ears demand sustained concentration, and regular practice teaches pupils that improvement comes from patient, repeated effort. These habits of focus and self-discipline carry over into other subjects, and research has associated musical training with stronger memory and language skills. As a result, children who play an instrument often approach homework and revision with greater persistence. A pupil who has spent months mastering a difficult piece, for example, learns that perseverance eventually produces results.

Furthermore, music contributes to emotional wellbeing and teamwork. Playing in a band or singing in a choir requires children to listen to others, adjust their own part and take shared responsibility for the final performance, so it fosters cooperation and mutual respect. Performing in front of an audience also builds self-confidence, and music gives young people a healthy way to express feelings and relieve stress. Admittedly, instruments and specialist teachers cost money, but schools can begin with inexpensive options such as singing and percussion. A shy pupil who gains confidence by performing in a school concert is likely to speak up more readily in other lessons.

In conclusion, I am convinced that music education benefits children by sharpening their concentration and by nurturing confidence and cooperation, and it should therefore remain part of every school's programme.

essays.question: Do the advantages of studying multiple languages outweigh the disadvantages? Give reasons and examples.

versions.text:
As globalisation brings people closer together, more and more students learn two or three foreign languages alongside their mother tongue. Although this requires considerable time and effort, I believe that the advantages outweigh the disadvantages.

On the positive side, studying several languages broadens career prospects and intellectual abilities. Multilingual graduates are able to work in international companies, deal directly with clients abroad and apply for positions in several countries, which gives them a clear advantage in a competitive labour market. Beyond employability, switching between languages exercises memory and attention, and learners often develop a deeper understanding of how language itself works, which makes each new language easier to acquire. They also gain access to literature, films and cultures in their original form, which promotes open-mindedness. For example, a student who speaks Spanish and French can read news and literature from dozens of countries without relying on translations.

On the negative side, mastering several languages demands a great deal of time and effort. Learners must spend hours on vocabulary and grammar, which may reduce the time available for other subjects, and confusion between similar languages is common. Moreover, adding language classes risks overloading a timetable that is already full. Nevertheless, these difficulties are manageable. Starting at primary level, when children absorb sounds and structures easily, spreads the workload over many years, and modern apps and online conversation partners make practice more flexible and enjoyable.

In conclusion, despite the heavy workload, learning several languages is, on balance, more beneficial than harmful, thanks to the career opportunities, mental agility and cultural understanding that it brings.

feedback.lexicalResource: Vốn từ vựng phong phú, sử dụng chính xác nhiều cụm từ hay liên quan đến chủ đề học ngôn ngữ và việc làm. Tuy nhiên, có thể bổ sung thêm một số cấu trúc từ vựng nâng cao hơn để đạt điểm cao hơn ở tiêu chí này.
